title: Fintech web, mobile and AI review workflow

facts: Synthetic regression fixture; not a saved job or delivered client system.

cover.footer: Illustrative product concept · fictional transactions and users.
cover.beat: Steve, I would start by agreeing one transaction journey before defining the wider platform. This sample follows a reconciliation exception through a shared web and mobile backend.

scenes.title: One backend for web and mobile
scenes.caption: Recommended architecture for the first sandbox transaction journey.
scenes.beat: Point to the shared backend. It validates provider events and checks user permissions before serving a record. The AI receives a redacted comparison; the reviewer approves a classification and the backend records it.
details: Recommended clients: React/Next.js for web and React Native for iOS/Android. Shared Node.js API and Postgres; OpenAI behind the backend.
Proposed access: MFA-backed sessions, server-side tenant/role checks, signed provider events and unique event IDs.
Proposed operations: sandbox integration tests, deployment checks, monitored retries, trace IDs and audited releases.

scenes.title: Review one exception, then approve its classification
scenes.caption: A custom transaction app with evidence, an AI suggestion and a local approval action.
scenes.beat: Point to TX-042 in the queue, then the 128-dollar provider record and 120-dollar invoice. Open the evidence. The eight-dollar difference is unexplained. Click Review again, then Approve classification. Jordan approves “Needs provider evidence”; the audit appears and reconciliation stays open.
details: The single transaction object supplies the queue, detail, derived difference and responsive mobile layout. No financial state is duplicated.
Use Show/Hide evidence for local inspection. Review again returns to the proposal; Approve classification records only local sample UI state.
The provider remains settled. Classification approval does not execute a transfer, adjust a ledger or resolve the reconciliation.
statuses: Jordan approved classification; reconciliation remains open

content.name: Reconcile
content.subtitle: One transaction requires a closer look.

transaction.description: Provider receipt differs from the expected invoice amount.

evidence.title: Provider receipt
evidence.detail: Settled receipt of $128.00. Signed sandbox event accepted; replay of this event creates no second record.

evidence.title: Invoice record
evidence.detail: Expected amount $120.00. No fee breakdown or adjustment evidence is attached.

analysis.summary: The $8.00 difference is unexplained. A fee is one possibility, but the available records do not establish the cause.
analysis.recommendation: Request the provider fee breakdown before assigning a cause or posting an adjustment.
analysis.dataBoundary: Surrogate transaction ID, amounts and redacted description. Account details, identity and provider credentials excluded.

decision.reason: Approved the evidence-needed classification. Your team must collect supporting details before resolving this exception.

close.title: Agree the product.
close.caption: Use a provider sandbox and representative exception cases before expanding the platform.

metrics.name: Exception handling time
metrics.definition: Median active reviewer minutes from opening an exception to recording a disposition. Compare the same sample cases against an agreed baseline.

metrics.name: Useful AI suggestions
metrics.definition: Share of suggestions reviewers mark useful and supported by available evidence. Record rejection reasons and test a held-out case set.

metrics.name: Duplicate safety
metrics.definition: Share of replay and retry test cases that preserve one transaction and one authorized state change. Check persisted IDs and audit events.

close.baselineNote: Agree baseline cases and acceptance thresholds in discovery. These are directional goals, not measured improvements.
